drills.q: Six friends face the CENTER of a circle. Is 'B's right' clockwise or anticlockwise from B?
drills.a: Facing center: left is anticlockwise, right is CLOCKWISE from the sitter. Facing OUTSIDE inverts both. The arrows get written on the circle before any positional clue.

drills.q: A row of five people faces SOUTH. The clue says 'Q is to the left of R.' Relative to the page, is Q left or right of R?
drills.a: Facing south REVERSES page-left/right: Q is to the page-RIGHT of R. The solver's perspective is never the reference -- the sitter's facing is, which is why the facing-direction arrow gets written above the row first.

drills.q: Solve: A is B's father. C is B's sister. D is C's son. How is D related to A?
drills.a: Grandson. Tree: A and B one generation link (father-son), C sibling of B, D child of C => two rows below A. Draw WHILE reading clause by clause; the verbal chain version mis-steps with no diagram to check.

drills.q: Ravi walks 10m north, turns right, walks 6m, turns left, walks 4m. Which direction is he facing, and how far is he from start?
drills.a: Facing NORTH (N -> right/East -> left/North). Displacement: (6, 14) => sqrt(36+196) = sqrt(232) ~= 15.2m. Facing is read off the last arrow; displacement needs the coordinate net. Options include 20m (sum of lengths) for the always-wrong pick.

drills.q: In a class A ranks 7th from top, 34th from bottom. How many students? And why minus 1?
drills.a: 7 + 34 - 1 = 40. A is counted in BOTH ranks, so subtract the double-count once. 41 is the off-by-one option always present.
First differences: 4, 6, 8, 10 => next diff 12 => 42. The difference engine resolves 80% of series mechanically; oscillating first diffs means split into two interleaved series.

drills.q: FRIEND is coded as GSJFOE. What is the rule, and what is CODED?
drills.a: Rule derived from the pair: +1 per letter. CODED -> DPEFE. Never guess from options -- derive the cipher from the given pair, then apply; position-based and reversal codes share the surface form.

drills.q: All engineers are graduates. Some graduates are managers. Does 'some engineers are managers' follow?
drills.a: No. The minimum legal Venn: engineers inside graduates; managers overlapping graduates but possibly missing engineers entirely. 'Some graduates are managers' does not place any manager inside the engineer region -- plausibility is not entailment.

drills.q: Angle between the hands at 3:40? State the formula and compute.
drills.a: theta = |30h - 11m/2| = |90 - 220| = 130 degrees. The signed result may need the 180-degree supplement check depending on which is asked. Hands coincide 22 times a day, not 24.

drills.q: You've spent 2 minutes on a seating puzzle and only placed two people. What do you do and why?
drills.a: Abandon full solve: switch to options-elimination against partial constraints, or skip. One stall costs three medium questions at the tail; 3 mediums beat 1 hard in points, every time. The 2-minute rule is triage, not defeat.

drills.q: 'Pointing to a photo, X says: he is the son of my grandfather's only son.' Who is in the photo?
drills.a: Grandfather's only son = X's father (only-son excludes uncles). Son of X's father = X or X's brother; 'he' + a photo implies the brother (or X himself). Unwind possessive chains one hop at a time on paper; gender-mark as you go.

drills.q: Why are syllogisms and series scheduled FIRST in a well-triaged attempt, not left for 'if time remains'?
drills.a: They're the fast questions (10-40s each with canned methods) -- guaranteed points. Slow seating puzzles first means the clock eats the sure things. Fast questions early is not a preference, it's the point distribution.
